slides.title: Establishing a Dynamic Multimodal HRI Dataset for Engagement Analysis with a Humanoid Robot
slides.highlight: This work proposes a structured protocol for a multimodal dataset integrating physiological signals and behavioral data to analyze user engagement. It is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Proposed experimental design for a multimodal HRI dataset to analyze user engagement across varying task complexities.
card.key_idea: A synchronized data architecture integrating human physiological signals (EDA, PPG), wearable/robot IMUs, RGB-D vision, and 15-item subjective questionnaires during collaborative object-handling tasks.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper describes a proposed protocol and planned recruitment of 30 participants, but provides no results.
card.limitation: The study is currently a conceptual design; data collection and implementation are listed as future work.

slides.title: Towards a Foundational Ontology for Identifying and Resolving Contradictions in Dialogue-based Human-Robot Interactions
slides.tldr: ONTOLOGY FOR RESOLVING HRI DIALOGUE CONTRADICTIONS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a foundational ontology (ATFOt) to formally represent and resolve contradictions in dialogue-based human-robot interactions, supporting the RwB goal of improving embodied social robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A foundational ontology for representing and resolving contradictions in dialogue-based human-robot and human-agent interactions.
card.key_idea: Uses METHONTOLOGY and Activity Theory to formally define contradictions (errors, conflicts, knowledge issues) via Set Theory, First Order Logic, and the Activity System Model.
card.evaluation: Preliminary results include formal definitions and principles; final evaluation will use qualitative studies, coverage, and competency questions in Protege.
card.limitation: The work is currently ongoing; full implementation and empirical validation of the ontology are not yet complete.

slides.title: Realbotix Testing Humanoid Robots at Live Events
slides.highlight: Realbotix is testing humanoid robots for crowd presentations, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: C$^{3}$T: Counterfactual Causal Reasoning for Sentiment Shifts in Social-Media Conversation Trees
slides.tldr: CAUSAL REASONING FOR SENTIMENT SHIFTS IN SOCIAL MEDIA
slides.highlight: This work introduces a thread-structured temporal model to analyze sentiment shifts and causal attributions in social-media conversations, supporting the societal-scale simulation goals of MIMIC.

card.one_liner: C³T models sentiment shifts in social-media conversation trees using counterfactual reasoning to attribute affective changes.
card.key_idea: A thread-structured Transformer that jointly predicts sentiment and shifts, utilizing intervention embeddings and a counterfactual loss to estimate the causal impact of specific discourse moves.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on public rumor datasets against neural and LLM baselines; C³T showed superior event-OOD robustness and causal ancestor attribution accuracy.
card.limitation: Causal analysis assumes conditional ignorability and treats cross-thread spillovers as a limitation.

slides.title: TEIDAN: A Multilingual Multiparty Dialogue Corpus
slides.highlight: This work introduces a multimodal corpus of triadic conversations that supports research on addressee recognition and turn-taking, aligning with HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: TEIDAN is a multilingual multimodal corpus of spontaneous three-party face-to-face discussions in Japanese and English.
card.key_idea: The corpus uses pin microphones, microphone arrays, and cameras to record triadic open-ended discussions, providing IPU-based transcripts for cross-linguistic analysis of turn-taking and grounding.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via descriptive quantitative statistics (IPU/pseudo-turn counts) and qualitative sequential analysis of turn construction across 69 sessions.
card.limitation: Differences in participant relationships (acquainted Japanese speakers vs. stranger English speakers) may confound cross-linguistic and cultural comparisons.

slides.title: Toward an Integrated Cognitive-Ergonomic Architecture for Human-Machine Interaction: Combining Cognitive Models with Human Factors Ergonomics
slides.highlight: This research proposes an integrated architecture combining cognitive models and ergonomics to analyze skill acquisition and adaptive behavior in industrial robotics, supporting the MOSAIC goal of estimating human proficiency and improving human-AI alignment.

card.one_liner: A new HMI architecture combining cognitive models with Human Factors Ergonomics for dynamic industrial environments.
card.key_idea: Synthesizes a tailored architecture from SOAR, ACT-R, LIDA, and COCOM to align decision-making and skill acquisition with ergonomic frameworks for human-centered interface design.
card.evaluation: Empirically grounded in industrial robotics applications focusing on operator expertise and real-time feedback loops; specific metrics not clearly stated.

slides.title: Agents That Model Agents: Five Principles Toward a Theory of Mind for 6G Networks
slides.tldr: THEORY OF MIND FOR RESILIENT MULTI-AGENT SYSTEMS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a Theory of Mind (ToM) framework for LLM agents to model peer beliefs and isolate hallucinations, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on inferring partner intent and self-correction via ToM.

card.one_liner: Proposes a Theory of Mind framework for 6G networks to prevent AI hallucinations from causing outages.
card.key_idea: Uses cellular sheaf theory and Bayesian inference to model peer beliefs, calculating trust as a 'Cognitive SNR' based on asserted precision versus second-order expectations.
card.evaluation: Validated via signaling-storm simulations using 1B-parameter telecom SLMs; cognitive SNR achieved AUC=1.000 in isolating a correct minority against a flawed majority.
card.limitation: Credible information capacity is strictly bounded by the alignment of agents' operational goals, regardless of physical bandwidth.

slides.title: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation through Human-AI Interaction
slides.highlight: This work proposes test-time adaptation through human-agent interaction (TAHI) to align agents with individual expertise, supporting ADAM-CHAT's goal of AI teammates that adapt at test time.

card.one_liner: TAHI adapts AI agents to individual expert standards using multi-session human-agent interaction signals.
card.key_idea: Integrates diverse interaction signals (plan edits, file changes, rubrics) via context induction (memory/skills) and weight adaptation (DPO on LoRA) with an evolving rubric module.
card.evaluation: Tested on 30 experts across 600 writing and visualization tasks; showed 4.5–20.9% solo success improvement over baselines with statistically significant gains.
card.limitation: Struggles to capture implicit situational judgment, such as context specificity and problem framing, compared to surface-level conventions.

slides.title: A Physics-Consistent Benchmark for Contact-Rich Human-Robot Interaction in Assistive Care
slides.highlight: This work introduces a benchmark for contact-rich assistive tasks, such as robot-assisted bathing, emphasizing physics-aware screening over simple task success. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A physics-consistent benchmark for assistive care showing that task completion doesn't guarantee physically valid contact.
card.key_idea: Combines a deformable, passively responding human model calibrated via manikin force-indentation measurements with physics-aware scoring and a leak-free, vision-only observation protocol.
card.evaluation: Evaluated State Machine, VoxPoser, and $\pi_{0.5}$ across 7 bathing tasks (140 runs/method) using peak force, joint-limit margins, and task success.
card.limitation: Uses a medical manikin instead of human tissue; upper-arm simulation reuses forearm calibration; limited to a single robotic-bathing scenario.

slides.title: When Robots Mishear Us: Mapping the Safety Risks of Voice-Controlled Embodied AI
slides.tldr: ASR ERRORS INCREASE EMBODIED AI SAFETY RISKS
slides.highlight: This research examines how automatic speech recognition errors can lead embodied AI to execute harmful instructions, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: ASR errors in voice-controlled embodied AI can bypass safety filters and trigger harmful physical actions.
card.key_idea: A framework simulating five ASR error types (e.g., acoustic substitution, noise) to test if corrupted instructions weaken model refusal and planning robustness in embodied AI.
card.evaluation: Tested Qwen2.5, GPT-4o-mini, and GPT-4.1-mini using POEX and SafeAgentBench. Results show increased acceptance of harmful tasks and decreased planning success rates.
card.limitation: Automatic ASR correction is not always effective, particularly when input semantics are heavily damaged by severe noise.

slides.title: AI as Teammate: Rethinking Task Distribution in Medical Training
slides.tldr: METACOGNITIVE FRAMEWORK FOR AI TASK ALLOCATION
slides.highlight: This paper proposes the SCAN framework to address AI misclassification through real-time metacognitive evaluation, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and adapting AI roles within human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: Reframes AI misuse in medical training as a 'misclassification' of task allocation relative to learner competence.
card.key_idea: The SCAN framework (Substitute, Complement, Aid, Non-Negotiable) uses Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development to guide AI task allocation and prevent skill failure.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper proposes a conceptual framework and a testable account rather than reporting empirical results.
card.limitation: Passive engagement in correctly classified tasks can lead to 'mis-skilling,' requiring human experts to act as epistemic auditors.

slides.title: Quiq Launches Voice Assist
slides.highlight: The launch of agentic AI that acts during live calls relates to ADAM-CHAT's focus on adaptive AI teammates for human-AI teaming.

slides.title: A Human-AI Theorem Connecting Spontaneous and Field-Induced Mechanisms of Collective Behavior in One Dimension
slides.tldr: HUMAN-AI COLLABORATION DISCOVERS STATISTICAL PHYSICS THEOREM
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how human-AI collaboration can generate scientific breakthroughs in statistical physics, supporting MIMIC's focus on integrating LLM-based agent models for complex system analysis.

card.one_liner: A human-AI collaboration proves a theorem mapping range-two 1D spin chains to simpler range-one chains.
card.key_idea: Uses a recursive Householder moving-frame transformation to map O(n) and Potts open chains with arbitrary inhomogeneous interactions to range-one chains with axial potentials.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via mathematical proof and mapping the frustrated J1-J2 model to the J-h field model; results are analytically exact.
card.limitation: The theorem specifically applies to open boundary conditions (OBC) in one-dimensional systems.

slides.title: Decoupling Turn-Taking from Semantics: A Decoupled Data Approach for Finite-State-Machine-Based Full-Duplex Dialogue
slides.tldr: DECOUPLED DATA APPROACH FOR FULL-DUPLEX DIALOGUE
slides.highlight: This work proposes a decoupled data approach and a Neural Finite State Machine framework to improve turn-taking naturalness in full-duplex dialogue. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and the perception of hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: Improves full-duplex dialogue by learning turn-taking from real human speech and semantics from text.
card.key_idea: A decoupled data approach using rule-based event-guided transformation of human-human dialogues and a Source-Aware Calibrated (SAC) Loss to balance rare state-transition tokens.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on Switchboard, Fisher, VoiceBench, and Full-Duplex-Bench. Results show significant F1 and semantic gains over synthetic-data NFSM baselines.
card.limitation: Loss of continuous-time information via discretization, lack of paralinguistic cues, and restriction to two-party QA dialogues.

slides.title: IRWOZ 2.0: A Large Language Model-driven Dialogue Dataset for Industrial Robot Conversations
slides.tldr: LLM-ENHANCED DIALOGUE DATASET FOR INDUSTRIAL HRI
slides.highlight: This work introduces IRWOZ 2.0, a refined dialogue dataset for industrial human-robot interaction, which is relevant to RwB's focus on AI-mediated embodied learning and HRI.

card.one_liner: IRWOZ 2.0 is an LLM-enhanced dialogue dataset improving state-tracking accuracy for industrial human-robot interactions.
card.key_idea: Combines Mistral and Claude-3.5 for automated error correction and structured dialogue generation across four industrial domains: Assembly, Delivery, Position, and Relocation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using GPT-2 variants; BLEU-4 scores rose from 0.1651 to 0.5604. Human evaluation by 23 experts confirmed high accuracy and naturalness.
card.limitation: Human evaluation indicated room for improvement in language variation and maintaining dynamic interaction flows during complex multi-step operations.

slides.title: From Siena to Beijing, the professor bringing humanoid touch to China
slides.highlight: The development of humanoid touch is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Alignment-Free Text-Audiobox for Voice Dubbing and Full-Duplex Dialogue Synthesis
slides.highlight: Text-AB enables high-quality full-duplex dialogue synthesis that natively models turn-taking, back-channeling, and emotional dynamics, supporting the multimodal social perception goals of HyECHO.

card.one_liner: Text-AB is a unified framework for high-quality voice dubbing and full-duplex dialogue synthesis without explicit alignment.
card.key_idea: A 3B-parameter Diffusion Transformer using flow-matching and DAC-VAE latent features, learning text-speech alignment via cross-attention instead of forced alignment or duration prediction.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via human MOS and objective metrics (WER, SpkSim) on internal dubbing and dialogue benchmarks; outperformed internal baselines in naturalness and similarity.
card.limitation: One-shot generation quality degrades notably beyond approximately one minute, requiring a multi-diffusion scheme for longer audio.

slides.title: Behavior--Realization Separation for Constrained Physical Human--Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: SEPARATING BEHAVIOR SPECIFICATION FROM CONSTRAINED REALIZATION IN pHRI
slides.highlight: This work proposes a layered architecture that separates desired behavior from constrained realization, improving workspace boundary adherence and torque feasibility in physical human-robot interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Proposed architecture separates desired interaction behavior from physical robot realization to improve constraint handling.
card.key_idea: A behavior layer provides desired acceleration; a predictive QP realization layer converts this into constrained commands, using a counterfactual audit to isolate constraint-driven errors.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via planar simulations and a 7-DOF Franka FR3 in MuJoCo; showed significantly lower workspace overshoot and torque budget violations than clipping.
card.limitation: The predictive QP runtime is currently validated only for memoryless affine behavior subclasses; nonlinear specifications may require different machinery.

slides.title: Social bots weaken activist cohesion
slides.highlight: This research examines how bot exposure disrupts human network ties and cohesion, providing insights into the social perception of group dynamics relevant to HyECHO.

card.one_liner: Social bot exposure during protest peaks erodes the human network cohesion necessary to sustain collective action.
card.key_idea: Analyzing 2020 BLM retweet networks, the authors measure triadic closure in ego networks and edge density in communities to link bot exposure to subsequent human tie decay.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using 2.5M tweets from 1M+ users; results were robust across three bot-probability thresholds and validated via GPT-3.5 stance classification.
card.limitation: The study focuses on a specific event (2020 BLM protests) and a single platform (X/Twitter), limiting generalizability across different contexts.

slides.title: Cooperative Risk-Aware Exploration in Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Systems Using Algorithmic Altruism
slides.tldr: ALTRUISTIC RISK DISTRIBUTION IN HETEROGENEOUS ROBOT TEAMS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a game-theoretic framework for risk-aware exploration where heterogeneous agents internalize the impact of their actions on teammates. This relates to HyECHO's focus on understanding the state and coordination of hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: A game-theoretic framework for multi-robot exploration where low-value robots altruistically accept higher risks for the team.
card.key_idea: Uses Hamilton's rule to shape utilities based on agent-specific value parameters, creating a weighted potential game that converges to Pareto-optimal trajectories via decentralized fictitious play.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulations and hardware experiments with wheeled robots; results showed reduced redundancy, improved robot separation, and risk reallocation while maintaining map coverage.
card.limitation: Global optimality and Pareto-optimality guarantees require the weighted potential function to be strictly jointly concave.

slides.title: Rethinking the Teacher-Student Framework for Test-Time Adaptation
slides.highlight: This work proposes an intransigent teacher approach to mitigate error accumulation during test-time adaptation, supporting ADAM-CHAT's goal of creating agents that adapt at test time.

card.one_liner: Using a fixed teacher instead of an EMA teacher prevents model collapse in long-sequence test-time adaptation.
card.key_idea: The 'Intransigent Teacher' (IT) freezes teacher weights ($ eta=1$), decoupling pseudo-label generation from student noise to stop the destructive positive feedback loop of error accumulation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on CIFAR10-C, ImageNet-C, DomainNet-126, and CCC using various architectures (ResNet, ViT, ConvNeXt). Results show significant accuracy gains and stability over long sequences.
card.limitation: Prioritizes stability over plasticity, which may hinder adaptation to rapid distribution shifts or over-regularize students in high-performing baseline scenarios.

slides.title: Dotting the Eye: An Intent-Driven Image Retouching Agent for Visual Focus Enhancement
slides.highlight: This work introduces EyeControl, an agent that aligns weak user intent with target editing regions to enhance visual focus, relating to MOSAIC's focus on aligning human-AI intent.

card.one_liner: EyeControl is an MLLM-driven agent that enhances visual focus in images using sparse user interaction cues.
card.key_idea: Combines a VLM planner for intent reasoning with a diffusion executor using Pseudo-Intention Attention Alignment (PAA) and an operation-consistency constraint for coordinated global-local adjustments.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the new ControlArt-Bench using PSNR, SSIM, and focus-specific metrics; outperformed existing agents and generative models in user preference studies.
